quote: Conceptually, we may call truth what we cannot change; metaphorically, it is the ground on which we stand and the sky that stretches above us.
source: Hannah Arendt, Truth and Politics, in Between Past and Future, closing sentence, p. 264 (Viking, 1968)

evidence.where: A page scan of the 1968 Viking edition covering pages 227 to 264 was opened and its text read. The sentence sits under the running head 264 Between Past and Future and is followed immediately by the title of the next essay, The Conquest of Space and the Stature of Man, which makes it the closing sentence of Truth and Politics. Wording independently corroborated by the Hannah Arendt Center at Bard.
evidence.edition: Between Past and Future: Eight Exercises in Political Thought, enlarged edition, Viking Press, 1968
evidence.locator: p. 264, the closing sentence of the essay

reason: Upgraded from the proposal’s HEDGE. The page the proposer could not open was opened: p. 264 is right, the punctuation is right, and the line turns out to be the essay’s closing sentence, which strengthens the fame test. Arendt stands at two for the year after this.
